name: Plasma scrubber
subtitle: a filter that strips ageing signals from blood

effects.effect: a learned model predicts a protein's 3D shape from its sequence
clearing out worn-out 'zombie' cells makes old mice healthier
big molecules trapped behind a membrane draw water in

effect: a learned model predicts a protein's 3D shape from its sequence
how: Joining an old mouse's circulation to a young one's makes the old mouse's muscle and brain behave younger, and simply diluting old blood does much of the same, which points at a handful of circulating proteins doing the harm. Designed binder proteins for those few can be fixed to beads in a column, so blood passes through and comes back missing them and nothing else. It is dialysis aimed at signals rather than waste.
obstacle: The list of proteins to remove is still guesswork, and stripping a signalling molecule you need could do real damage.
why: Plasma dilution works in mice; which factors to pull is still unknown.
real: A 2025 proteomics study showed pore-size-based therapeutic apheresis lowers several age-associated plasma proteins, and a patent proposes columns for 'pro-aging' factors beyond the existing Kaneka Lixelle beta-2-microglobulin column, but no designed-binder affinity column targeting specific ageing factors has been demonstrated.
